statement.p: The domain of the function h graphed below is all real numbers, and all of its extreme values occur when -3\lt x\lt 3. Use the graph to answer the following questions.

description.p: Graph of a continuous function h in the coordinate plane. In the visible window, the function increases from the point (-3,-3) to (-2.5,-2), where there is horizontal tangent line, and then increases again to (-2,-1). At this point there is a sharp corner and the graph is decreasing to (0,-2), which has a sharp corner. From here the graph is increasing to (1,2). Here the graph resembles the vertex of a parabola, and smoothly turns around, decreasing to (1.5,1). Here there is another sharp corner as the function continues decreasing. The end behavior suggested by the graph is h(x)\to-\infty as x\to\pm\infty.

statement.p: Identify all of the values of c for which h(c) is a local maximum of h. If there is more than one value, enter the values as a comma-separated list. If there are none, enter DNE.
Identify all of the values of c for which h(c) is a local minimum of h. If there is more than one value, enter the values as a comma-separated list. If there are none, enter DNE.
Does h have a global maximum? If so, enter the value of its global maximum. If there is no global maximum, enter DNE.
Does h have a global minimum? If so, enter the value of its global minimum. If there is no global minimum, enter DNE.
Identify all of the values of c for which h'(c)=0. If there is more than one value, enter the values as a comma-separated list. If there are none, enter DNE.
Identify all of the values of c for which h'(c) does not exist. If there is more than one value, enter the values as a comma-separated list. If there are none, enter DNE.

True or false: every relative maximum and minimum of h occurs at a point where h'(c) is either zero or does not exist.
?
True
False

True or false: at every point where h'(c) is zero or does not exist, h has a relative maximum or minimum.
?
True
